sheet-2.description: The central business district of Bound Brook, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The sheet runs along East Main Street from Mountain Avenue at the left to East Street at the right edge, with East High Street along the top and East 2nd Street across the middle. Maiden Lane and Hamilton run north from East Main between the blocks. The north side of East Main is a continuous row of two and three storey brick stores, most of them drawn in pink, among them the Bound Brook Trust Co., a public hall, the Berkley Hotel, the Brook Theatre, a post office and a plumbing shop. Behind them lie dwellings, an Elks club and lodge rooms, a state office, the offices of a newspaper and a fire department ladder company. The Public Library stands at the top right on the Hamilton Street block. At the right the Runyon-Field Lumber Co. fills a long block with lumber storage sheds and a planing mill, next to a cemetery. South of East Main the sheet shows a second row of stores, a bank, the Public Service Corp'n car barns and the Somerset Supply Co., then the passenger station and the wide tracks of the C.R.R. of N.J., the L.V.R.R. and the P. & R. R.R. The Apgar Coal & Grain Co. coal pockets appear at the lower right. The compass rose at the upper right is turned, so the streets run at a slight angle to the page. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 9 to the north, 6 and 4 to the west, 3 to the east and 11 and 18 to the south.
notes: In OpenStreetMap East Main, East 2nd and East High keep their names (East Main Street, East 2nd Street, East High Street); Hamilton is Hamilton Street, and the East 2nd and East Main junctions also carry Hamilton Boulevard; East is East Street.
The sheet's right edge cuts East Street along its western edge, so East Street junctions are not used here.
Bound Brook: East Main Street from Mountain Avenue to East Street, Maiden Lane, Hamilton; 50 ft; one part.

sheet-3.description: The eastern end of the East Main Street corridor in Bound Brook, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. East Street runs down the left edge, and East High Street, East 2nd Street and East Main run away from it to the right at a slight upward slope. The block between East High and East 2nd holds a row of small frame dwellings on narrow lots numbered 514 to 543, with another row of dwellings fronting East Street. Between East 2nd and East Main stand the Runyon Field Lumber Co. sheds, the Pillar of Fire Church school and dormitories, drawn in blue, and the Bound Brook Hotel on the corner of East Street. East of the church the land is largely open and unbuilt. At the foot of the sheet East Main curves down to Main (Easton Rd.), which crosses the broad railroad corridor of the C.R.R. of N.J., the P. & R. R.R. and the L.V.R.R. on a bridge. A garage with a show room and vulcanizing shop, a filling station and the Bound Brook Hose Co. No. 1 fire station with its hose tower stand near the approach. South of the tracks are a freight house, a passenger station, the Apgar Coal & Grain Co. and, at the right, The Ruberoid Co. flooring plant (Mutual Risk), with its machine rooms, asphalt storage tanks and unloading house. The bottom edge is labelled for the Raritan River. The compass rose at the upper right shows north turned a few degrees from the page vertical. Neighbouring sheets are 2 to the west, 9, 16 and 17 to the north and 18 and 38 to the south.
notes: Main (Easton Road) is South Main Street (CR 527) in OpenStreetMap; East High, East 2nd, East Main and East keep their names with Street added.
A street name printed only as ROAD runs along the lower right; the preceding word is not on this sheet.

Placed by three hand-picked points along East Street only (a two-parameter fit); rotation and scale are low confidence. The modern Bolmer Boulevard junction at East 2nd and East Street lies 10.7 m from the right-of-way centre used.
Bound Brook: East Street to Main Street (Easton Road) and the railroad corridor; 50 ft; one part. Placed from three hand-picked points on East Street (helmert); low confidence.

sheet-4.description: A residential district in the west of Bound Brook, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. West High Street runs along the top of the sheet and West 2nd Street crosses it above the middle. Vosseller Avenue forms the left side, curving to the north-west at the top, with Van Keuren Avenue and Fairview Avenue running down the page parallel to it. Linden Avenue and Talmage Avenue cross the lower part. Nearly all the buildings are frame dwellings of one to two and a half storeys on deep lots, with sheds, barns and outbuildings behind them, and a few built with pink brick or stone walls. The Slavish Club stands on the east side of Vosseller Avenue. Near the bottom right, between Linden and Talmage Avenues, a larger tile or brick building with blue annexes and a row of small frame stores occupy a block numbered 39. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches are drawn in the streets. Block numbers 41A, 41B, 42, 40A and 39 are printed in the blocks. The compass rose is at the right edge. The adjoining sheets are numbered 12 to the north, 5 to the east, 10 to the south and 11 to the west, where Pine Street leaves Vosseller Avenue.
notes: Vosseller Avenue, Van Keuren Avenue, Fairview Avenue, Linden Avenue, Talmage Avenue, West High Street and West 2nd Street keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
The modern Fairview Avenue is straighter than the street drawn here; the Fairview Avenue and West High Street junction in OpenStreetMap was not used.
Bound Brook: Vosseller to Fairview Avenue, West High to Talmage; 50 ft; faint scan (ink_below_paper 80); one part.

sheet-5.description: A residential and school district on the west side of Bound Brook, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. Winsor Street crosses the sheet on a diagonal from the top towards the lower left, carrying a 6 inch water pipe, and meets West High Street at the top and West 2nd Street and Linden Avenue lower down. West High Street and West 2nd Street run down to the right at a steep slope. Fairview Avenue is the street at the left edge. Linden Avenue and Talmage Avenue run across the lower part of the sheet, and Drake Street closes the block at the lower right. The La Fayette Public School, a large pink brick building with heating, lights and chemical extinguishers noted, stands between Winsor Street and West High Street. Most other buildings are frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with a few small shops along Talmage Avenue, where a garment factory, a bake shop, a drug store and a pink brick building are drawn. A cider mill and a poultry building appear in the blocks at the left. Shunpire Street leaves Talmage Avenue near the bottom. Block numbers 41C, 40B, 7 1/2, 7D, 7B, 7A and 39 are printed. The compass rose at the top right points almost straight up. Neighbouring sheets are 12 to the north, 7 to the north-east, 6 to the east, 10 to the south and 4 to the west.
notes: Winsor Street, West High Street, West 2nd Street, Linden Avenue, Talmage Avenue, Drake Street and Fairview Avenue keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
Winsor Street south of West High Street (the diagonal street with the water pipe) is not in the OpenStreetMap network, nor is Shunpire Street.
Bound Brook: Winsor Street, La Fayette Public School, Linden and Talmage Avenues, Drake Street; 50 ft; ink 80; one part. Shunpire St. printed (Shunpike / Columbus Place).

sheet-6.description: The centre of Bound Brook between West High Street and the railroad, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. Church Street and John Street run from the top of the sheet down to East Main and West Main, with West 2nd Street and East 2nd Street crossing them at the middle of the top half, and Mountain Avenue at the right edge. Church Street shifts at East 2nd Street, so its lower half is the street running diagonally down to the left of John Street. The top rows of blocks are filled with frame dwellings and outbuildings. St. Joseph's R.C. Church, drawn in blue, stands with its parochial school, rectory and convent between East 2nd Street and East Main near Mountain Avenue. A fire department building, a Masonic Temple and rows of dwellings lie between Church and John Streets. At the foot of the blocks the large Verplex Embossing & Finishing Co. building, tenant of a clothing factory, and the L. D. Cook & Co. lumber and millwork yard with its storage sheds fill the area along East Main and West Main. Lime and cement warehouses and a freight house of the C.R.R. of N.J. stand beside the railroad yard at the lower right, with the Somerset Supply Company feed, hay and grain building at the edge. At the left, Drake and Talmage Avenue meet in a small group of lots with a bottling shop and an auto repair shop. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 7, 8, 5, 6, 9, 10, 2 and 7C.
notes: Church, John and Mountain Avenue keep their names (Church Street, John Street) in OpenStreetMap; East and West High, 2nd and Main are East High Street, West High Street and so on.
Church Street meets East 2nd Street in two places 39 m apart in OpenStreetMap, the upper (West 2nd) and lower (East 2nd) street sections, both drawn here.
The drawn Raritan Valley (C.R.R. of N.J.) tracks lie about 24 m from the modern line.
Bound Brook: Church and John Streets between West High and Main; 50 ft; one part.

sheet-7.description: Residential blocks in the centre of Bound Brook, north of the business district, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The sheet covers the two blocks between West Union Avenue at the top and West High Street at the bottom, bounded on the west by Winsor Street and on the east by Church Street, with West Franklin Street crossing the middle. The short ends of East Union Avenue, East Franklin Street and East High Street are lettered beyond Church Street at the right edge, where the next sheet takes over. Almost every building is a frame dwelling, most of two storeys, set in a regular row of narrow lots facing the cross streets; the lots along West Union Avenue are deep and the rear halves hold sheds, poultry houses and a few small outbuildings. A disused carpenter shop stands behind the West Union Avenue lots in the upper block. The only institution on the sheet is the Congregational Church at the north-west corner of Church Street and West High Street, a brick-veneered building drawn in pink and yellow. Water pipes are shown in Winsor Street, West Union Avenue, West Franklin Street and Church Street, with hydrants at several corners and a fire alarm box at Church and West Franklin. A block number, 51, is printed in the northern block. The sheet's edges carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets: 13 to the north, 12 to the west, 8 to the east and 5 and 6 to the south. The north arrow is at the left edge; the streets run roughly east to west across the page.
notes: Winsor, Church, West Union Avenue, West Franklin Street and West High Street keep their names in OpenStreetMap (Winsor Street, Church Street).
Congregational Church at Church Street and West High Street.
Bound Brook: West Union Avenue to West High Street between Winsor and Church; 50 ft. Pilot sheet; one part.

sheet-8.description: Residential blocks in the centre of Bound Brook, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The sheet lies east of Sheet 7 and covers the ground between East Union Avenue at the top and East High Street at the bottom, running from Church Street at the left, through John Street, to Mountain Avenue at the right edge. East Franklin Street crosses the middle of the sheet and ends before Mountain Avenue. The built-up lots are mostly frame dwellings of one or two storeys with sheds and small outbuildings at the rear, standing on narrow lots between Church and John Streets. East of John Street the lots are deeper and more sparsely built, and the large blocks along East Union Avenue hold only a handful of houses and outbuildings. The institutions are grouped on East Franklin Street: St. Paul's Episcopal Church, a brick building drawn in pink, with its parish house beside it, and, at the corner of Church Street, the fire department building of the Watchung Fire Co. No. 3. An auto sales and service garage with room for twelve cars stands on the east side of John Street, and another brick building stands near Mountain Avenue in the lower right. Water pipes of four to ten inches run in the streets, with hydrants at most corners and fire alarm boxes at Church Street and at Mountain Avenue. A compass rose and north arrow are at the upper left, and the streets run roughly east to west across the page. The margins give the numbers of the adjoining sheets: 13 to the north, 7 to the west, 9 to the east and 6 to the south. The January 1927 Bound Brook cartouche is at the upper right and the scale bar at the foot.
notes: East Franklin, East High, Church and John are lettered without a suffix; today East Franklin Street, East High Street, Church Street and John Street.
St. Paul's Episcopal Church and parish house on East Franklin Street; Watchung Fire Co. No. 3 at Church Street.
Bound Brook: East Union Avenue to East High Street between Church Street and Mountain Avenue; 50 ft; one part.

sheet-9.description: Residential blocks east of Sheet 8 in Bound Brook, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. East Union Avenue runs across the top of the sheet, Somerset across the middle and East High at the bottom; the north-south streets are Mountain Avenue, which runs obliquely from the upper centre to the lower left edge, Hamilton in the middle of the sheet, and a street lettered East, which runs diagonally from the upper right towards the lower right. A short street, Maiden Lane, leaves East High at the bottom left. Almost all the buildings are frame dwellings of one or two storeys with small outbuildings, standing on narrow lots; the row along the north side of East Union Avenue, numbered in the 400s, has small auto houses about 15 ft to the rear. A pink brick building and a few small yellow frame buildings stand on Hamilton Street between Somerset and East Union. The blocks are numbered 54 and 55 at the centre, 56 at the right edge and 57 at the top, and the numbers of the neighbouring sheets are printed at the margins: 13 to the north, 8 to the west and 2 and 3 to the south. Water pipes run in Mountain Avenue, Hamilton Street, East Union Avenue, Somerset and East High, with a hydrant at nearly every corner and fire alarm boxes on Mountain Avenue and on East Union Avenue. The lower part of the sheet is drawn with lots cut by the oblique line of the East street, whose edge makes the blocks at the lower right wedge-shaped. The compass rose is at the upper left and the January 1927 Bound Brook cartouche is at the top right; the scale bar is at the foot.
notes: Hamilton, Somerset and East are lettered without a suffix; today Hamilton Street, Somerset Street and East Street.
Mountain Avenue meets East High Street at the extreme left edge of the sheet; that junction is just off the scan.
Bound Brook: Mountain Avenue to East Street between East Union Avenue and East High Street (Hamilton, Somerset); 50 ft; one part.

sheet-10-1.description: The west side of Bound Brook along Talmage Avenue, the railroad and West Main, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 80 degrees on the page, so that the streets which run east and west on the ground run up and down the sheet. Talmage Avenue forms the left side of the sheet and carries a long row of narrow lots with frame dwellings, a few brick stores and the Washington House, a brick hotel at the point where Shunpike leaves Talmage Avenue obliquely. A fire department building, the Relief Hose Co. No. 4, stands in the lower half of Talmage Avenue, and Vosseller Avenue crosses the foot of the sheet. Van Heuren Avenue enters Talmage Avenue from the left. West Main runs down the middle, parallel to and west of the railroad; between Shunpike and West Main a large auto show room and service building, drawn in blue, is set in a triangular block. A broad band of railroad tracks, labelled for the C.R.R. of N.J. and the P. & R. R.R., crosses the whole height of the sheet with a coal trestle at the upper centre, a section house and a concrete flagman's shanty. East of the tracks, at the upper right, are the buildings of Middlebrook Mills, Inc., manufacturers of woolen cloth: the main mill, finishing and designing, dye house, engine room, wash and rug storehouse, blend storehouse and wool storehouses, with their own water mains and a printed note on night watchman, power and fire protection. The block numbers 6, 36 and 45 and the sheet numbers 4, 5, 6 and 10 are printed at the margins. A boxed area at the lower right is a separate part of the sheet and is not covered by this mask. The compass rose is east of the mills.
notes: Shunpike appears to be today's Columbus Place, which leaves Talmage Avenue at the same oblique angle (identified from the junction positions, not from a printed name).
Van Heuren Avenue is lettered with this spelling; OpenStreetMap has Van Keuren Avenue.
West Main is lettered without a suffix; today West Main Street. Its modern line sits several metres from the drawn street at its northern end, so only the Vosseller Avenue junction is used.
Part 2, the boxed area at the lower right, is not georeferenced.

Bound Brook: Talmage Avenue, West Main, railroad, Middlebrook mills; 50 ft; turned (north to the left). Part 1 a two-point helmert (Vosseller at Talmage and West Main); Talmage, Van Keuren and Columbus Place (Shunpike) look displaced and were left out. Part 2 (lower right box) not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: box lower right: West Main yard and Bound Brook Supply Co. (no street junction; needs step 6b points carried from sheet 5 or 6).

sheet-11-1.description: A residential district of western Bound Brook, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 11 degrees from the page, covering the ground between West High at the top and West Main at the bottom, and from Thompson Avenue at the left edge to Vosseller Avenue at the right. The streets that run across the sheet are Evergreen Avenue, West High, West 2nd Street, Wheatland Avenue and Talmage Avenue; the cross streets are Thompson Avenue, Park Pl., Ware Ct., Hardy Avenue, Lamonte Avenue, Romney Rd., North, Fisher Avenue and Vosseller Avenue, with New Hampshire La. and Pine as shorter streets. The upper left is mostly subdivided blocks with no buildings (blocks 237 to 239 and 240 to 243) and Codrington Park at the top. In the upper centre stand The Evergreens, a home for the aged, and the grounds of a large house at the head of St. John's Pl. The densest development is around West 2nd Street, Lamonte Avenue, Romney Rd. and North, where the small frame dwellings, many in brick and pink, press close together. At the right are St. Mary's R.C. Church (Polish) with its parochial school and church, the LaMonte Public School with St. Mary's Church beside it, and a green house. A wide band of railroad tracks, labelled for the C.R.R. of N.J., crosses the lower part of the sheet from left to right, with the block number 36 1/2; below it West Main carries another row of dwellings. A boxed inset of the Bound Brook Water Co. pumping station occupies the lower left corner and is not covered by this mask. The cartouche of January 1927 is at the upper right and the scale bar at the foot.
notes: Several names are lettered without a suffix (West High, North, Pine, West Main); today West High Street, North Street, Pine Street and West Main Street.
Ware Court is drawn about 25 m from its modern line and was left out of the fit.
Part 2, the Bound Brook Water Co. pumping station inset at the lower left, is not georeferenced.

Bound Brook west end: West High to West Main, Thompson Avenue to Vosseller Avenue; 100 ft. Part 1 main; part 2 (inset lower left, Bound Brook Water Co. pumping station, Middle Brook) not placed. Ware Court drawn about 25 m off its modern line, left out.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset lower left: Bound Brook Water Co. pumping station on Talmage Avenue, Middle Brook, steel bridge (one street, no junction; needs step 6b points carried from sheet 4 or 5).

sheet-12.description: The west side of the town centre of Bound Brook between Winsor Street and Vosseller Avenue, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 16 degrees on the page. Four main streets run across the sheet from lower left to upper right: Cherry Avenue at the top, West Maple, West Union and, below them, West Franklin and West High, which close the sheet at the bottom. Winsor forms the right edge. The cross streets are Carleton, Washington, Hayward and Livingston Av., which run down the page, and Vosseller Avenue, which cuts diagonally across the lower left from Grove Av. and Longwood Av. to West High. The upper left is mainly subdivided but unbuilt ground, with long narrow lots and block numbers 207 to 221. The blocks between West Maple and West High are closely built with small frame dwellings along the avenues. The institutions are Washington High School, a large brick building drawn in pink with auditorium and gymnasium, at the right of the middle; St. Johns Evangelical Lutheran Church and a Methodist Episcopal church on West Union Avenue; the Bound Brook Inn, on the south side of West Union at the centre; and a filling station near the junction of Vosseller Avenue and Longwood Av. A short street, St. John's Pl., runs southward at the lower left. The sheet numbers 13 to the north, 7 to the east, 5 and 4 to the south and 11 to the west are printed at the margins, with block numbers 46 to 49 and 216. The compass rose is in the upper centre and the scale bar at the foot.
notes: Winsor, Carleton, Washington, Hayward, West Franklin and West High are lettered without a suffix; today Winsor Street, Carleton Street, Washington Street, Hayward Street, West Franklin Street and West High Street.
Livingston Av. is today Livingston Street.
Washington Street at West Union Avenue was rejected as an outlier in the fit (15.6 m).
Bound Brook north-west: Cherry Avenue to West High Street, Winsor Street to Vosseller Avenue; 100 ft; one part.

sheet-13-1.description: Residential streets in the north-western part of Bound Brook, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The part covers the whole sheet except the inset at its top left. West Maple Avenue and East Maple Avenue cross the lower third of the page, and West Union Avenue and East Union Avenue run along the bottom edge, where the next sheets (7, 8 and 9) are numbered. Windsor and Central Avenue run up the left half of the page, Church up the middle, and Watchung Road and Mountain Avenue up the right, all tilted a few degrees off vertical. Chestnut crosses the upper left. At the top Piedmont Drive curves round from the left edge to meet Watchung Road, and a looping street system of Wahnetah Drive and a second stretch of Watchung Road fills the block between Church and Mountain Avenue. Almost every building is a frame dwelling of one or two storeys with a small outbuilding behind it; blocks 104, 105 and 210 on the left and 246, 106 and 107 at the top are mostly open land with only a few houses, and several lots are lettered as having no exposure. The larger buildings are the First Presbyterian Church with its basketball court and Sunday school at the corner of East Union Avenue, and the Middlebrook Country Club building on the loop east of Watchung Road. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches and hydrants are marked in most streets. A compass rose and cemetery lettering lie at the right edge, and a scale bar of 100 ft stands at the middle of the page. The inset at the top left, the King Chemical Company works, is a separate part.
notes: The street printed Windsor is Winsor Street in OpenStreetMap.
The street printed Church is Church Street today; Central Avenue, Chestnut and Mountain Avenue are unchanged apart from the suffix.
Chestnut is drawn about 38 ft wide, narrower than today's right-of-way, and jogs where it crosses Windsor.
Windsor between West Maple Avenue and West Union Avenue is drawn 30 ft wide and its modern line is about 9 m from the drawn junction with West Union Avenue, so that junction is not used.
The inset King Chemical Co. works (top left) is not georeferenced: it has no street junction.

Bound Brook north: Windsor (printed so here, Winsor on sheets 5 and 7), Church, Chestnut, Mountain Avenue, Watchung Road, Piedmont and Wahnetah Drives; 100 ft. Part 1 main (street_widths Chestnut 38 ft); part 2 (inset top left, King Chemical Co. works) not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset top left: King Chemical Co. works (no street junction; needs identification of the site and parcel corners (step 6b)).

sheet-14.description: The north-east corner of South Bound Brook, on the south bank of the Raritan River and the Delaware and Raritan Canal, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. The top of the sheet is taken up by the river, a strip of land between river and canal carrying a storage warehouse, small sheds and a road, and the canal with its concrete bulkhead. A steel bridge carries Main (marked Easton Road) across canal and river at the top left. South of the canal, the Ruberoid Company's roofing plant fills the upper right: a long manufacturing building with a boiler house, a pump house, oil furnaces, a heating house, tanks and large storage warehouses, drawn in pink and yellow with a block of notes on its power, watchmen and fire protection at the right edge. A second Ruberoid works, the paint and tape plant, stands along Canal Road at the left. Main runs diagonally from the bridge to the lower right. Along it, and in the blocks between it and Clinton, stand the post office, a fire department and borough hall, an automobile repair shop, the Reformed Church of Bound Brook with its Sunday school, and frame dwellings. Below Clinton the sheet shows houses in blocks 22A and 23 and open, subdivided lots along Earl and Prospect, with a club house and bowling alleys near Cedar. Water pipes are lettered in most streets. The north arrow at the lower right points up and to the right, so the streets run at an angle to the page. Sheets 15 and 16 are numbered at the left and lower right, and a scale bar is at the foot.
notes: The bridge approach is lettered Main (Easton Rd.).
Main, Canal Road, Elm, Clinton, Elizabeth and Cedar correspond to Main Street, Canal Road, Elm Street, Clinton Street, Elizabeth Street and Cedar Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Bell Place is Bell Street today.
The OpenStreetMap node where Clinton Street meets Main Street (Canal Crossing) lies about 150 m from the drawn junction, so Main's junctions with Clinton, Elm and Cedar are not used.
Prospect Street (OpenStreetMap) meets Bell Street and Cedar Avenue along the street lettered Earl here.
South Bound Brook: Main Street at the bridge, Canal Road, Ruberoid works; 50 ft; one part. Control only west and south; Canal Road / Main Street hand-picked.

sheet-15.description: The centre of South Bound Brook, on the south side of the Delaware and Raritan Canal, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. The Raritan River and the canal, with a lock, cross the top left corner, and Canal Road runs along the canal bank from the lower left to the top right. Between it and Clinton lie the lumber sheds and yard of Starts Lumber Co. and a row of small dwellings; a warehouse and sheds of the Ruberoid Co. stand at the top. South of Clinton the blocks are laid out on a grid of Madison, Elizabeth, Prospect, Nassau and High, with a bottling works in block 153. Elizabeth, the main street, runs from the canal to the school at High, and near it stand the South Bound Brook Public School and a fire alarm box at the corner of High. Block 165 is the baseball grounds, and several large blocks, 164, 166 and 475, are almost empty of buildings and cut into long narrow lots. At the right, Earl, Cottage Place, Prospect Place and Bell Place lie in a small area of newly laid out lots with the Winberg Mfg. Co. tent and awning factory at its east end. The streets run at an angle to the page, and the north arrow at the right points up and to the left. The sheet joins sheet 14 to the north east and sheet 16 to the east, and the lower edge carries a 100 ft scale bar. Block numbers 149 to 154, 163 to 166 and 473 to 476 are printed.
notes: Alexander Avenue, Madison, Elizabeth, Nassau, High and Cedar correspond to streets of the same name in OpenStreetMap; Shield Avenue is Shields Avenue and Bell Place is Bell Street today.
Prospect is drawn with a jog at Madison, about 33 m, matching the offset between Prospect Street and West Prospect Street in OpenStreetMap.
The junctions of High with Shield Avenue and of Edgewood Terrace with Van Sickle Boulevard lie 4 to 5 m from the fit and are not used.
Egbert Avenue and East Jefferson Street were read at low resolution and may be mis-read.
South Bound Brook: Canal Road to Van Sickle Boulevard, Clinton to Madison; 100 ft; one part.

sheet-16-1.description: The eastern half of South Bound Brook, between the village centre and the Delaware and Raritan Canal, drawn at 100 ft to an inch. Main runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right and carries the long fronts of the blocks on either side of it. North and east of it a second grid of streets set at right angles to it, Washington, Warren, Montgomery, Franklin and Jackson, runs down to a street lettered Canal along the canal bank, with narrow lots numbered along each. Johnson Street crosses at the lower right. The canal and, at the top right, the Raritan River cross the upper right corner. To the west the blocks follow the older grid: Cherry, Warren and Maple Avenue run up and down the page and High, East Jefferson, Noble, Munro, Sturr and Steward cross them, with Cedar along the left edge. Dwellings are mostly small frame houses, scattered irregularly in the northern blocks. The public school stands on Warren at about the middle of the left side, and St. Paul's M.E. Church (Colored) at the corner of East Jefferson. Large areas on the right, blocks 182, 184 and 185, are almost empty. A compass rose and a scale bar of 100 ft stand at the foot. A heavy-lined area at the lower right, part of block 185, is a separate inset and is not part of this one. Sheets 14 and 15 are numbered at the left.
notes: Steward is Stewart Street in OpenStreetMap.
East Jefferson is Jefferson Street today, and the street lettered Canal along the canal is Canal Street.
Egbert Avenue and Earl Street are read from small lettering at the left edge and may be mis-read.
The inset at the lower right (block 185 with a canal bend, no street junction) is not georeferenced.
South Bound Brook east: Main, Washington, Warren, Montgomery, Franklin to the canal; 100 ft. Part 1 main; part 2 (inset lower right, part of block 185 at a canal bend) not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset lower right: part of block 185 with a canal bend (no street junction; needs parcel corners (step 6b)).

sheet-17-1.description: The main part of sheet 17 covers the western end of East Bound Brook in the Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, at 50 ft to an inch, with north towards the top. Raritan Avenue runs diagonally up the left side, 2nd Street crosses the top, A Street bounds the right edge and Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet; the numbered lots 101 to 112 along the north side of 2nd Street are mostly vacant, with a few small frame dwellings. Between 2nd Street and Main Street the sheet shows the Roto Engraving and Printing Co. (printing, engraving and paper warehouse buildings), a shop of the Research Corporation (electrical precipitation), the Pierce Estates tile-roofed buildings, and a brine warehouse of the Causse Manufacturing and Importing Co. South of Main Street stand the works of Archer and Baldwin (dynamos and motors, with fire ruins), the Watson Bros. Machine Co. cordage machinery shop, the Vac. factory buildings of the Pierce Estates, and the large Causse preserved-fruits factory. Below them lie the Central Railroad of New Jersey, Philadelphia and Reading and Lehigh Valley lines, and at the bottom the long raised-roof works of the Pierce Estates, formerly American Engineering and Electric Co., marked vacant and for sale. Water pipes run along the streets and a dashed 6 inch pipe crosses the bottom. A small inset at the top left, a detached piece of Main Street with Cook's Transportation Line garage, is a separate part and is not included here.
notes: Main is now Walnut Street and 2nd Street is now Maple Street in the modern street data; A Street keeps its name.
Raritan Avenue is drawn about 45 m west of the modern Raritan Avenue at Main Street, so it was not used as control.
Placed from only two junctions on A Street at the right edge (a two-point helmert); scale and rotation agree with sheet 18.

East Bound Brook (Middlesex): Main (Walnut Street), Raritan Avenue, A Street; 50 ft. Part 1 a two-point helmert on A Street; Raritan Avenue left out (modern node about 45 m from the drawn junction). Part 2 (inset top left, Cook garage) not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset top left: Cook garage, detached piece of Main Street (its only junction is hidden under the heavy line; needs a hand pick carried from sheet-17-1 (step 6b)).

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows the central part of East Bound Brook in the Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, at 50 ft to an inch, with north towards the top. The streets form a grid: A, B, C and D Streets run north and south, 2nd Street crosses near the top and Main Street crosses the middle, with the railroad corridor below. North of Main Street the blocks hold small frame dwellings and a fire house of the H. C. Pierce Hose Co., and in the middle block the large Pathe Freres Bound Brook laboratory, with film storage, negative vaults, developing and drying buildings and its own fire hose stations. South of Main Street are the Fischer-Sweeny Bronze Co. Inc. (bronze and aluminum castings) with foundries Nos. 9 and 10 and warehouse No. 8, the buildings of the former Crown Chemical Corp'n, and a block of dwellings on the right. The three railroad lines, the Central Railroad of New Jersey, Philadelphia and Reading and Lehigh Valley, cross below, with C Street carried over them on a frame viaduct. Beyond the tracks are the Chipman Chemical Co. insecticide works, the Paris Green and arsenic acid factories, fire ruins and, at the lower right, the Pierce Estates' concrete warehouses L5 to L8.
notes: Main is now Walnut Street and 2nd Street is now Maple Street in the modern street data.
The sheet is drawn at 7.97 px/ft, in line with the 7.96 of the other 50 ft sheets of the atlas.
C Street continues south over the tracks on an Approach to Viaduct; the modern grid south of Main is not drawn as streets on this sheet.
East Bound Brook (Middlesex): A to D Streets, 2nd Street (Maple Street), Main (Walnut Street); 50 ft; one part.

sheet-19-1.description: The upper part of sheet 19 covers the northern end of East Bound Brook in the Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, at 100 ft to an inch. North is towards the top, tilted a little to the left. Raritan Avenue curves along the left side beside Ambrose Brook, which cuts across the top left corner. A regular grid of platted streets fills the sheet: A, B, C, D and E Streets run north and south, crossed by 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets, with 5th Street meeting a diagonal street at the top right. The blocks are divided into narrow numbered lots, some carrying the lot numbers 901 to 925, and nearly all are vacant. Only a scatter of small frame dwellings stand along Raritan Avenue and in the blocks beside 3rd Street, and the Pierce Public School, a brick building heated by steam and lit by electricity, stands between A Street and B Street north of 3rd Street. The strip along the bottom above the heavy line repeats the top blocks of sheets 17 and 18, which are marked at the lower edge. Four water pipes of 4 inch bore follow the streets. A separate part below the heavy line shows Harris Avenue and the nursery grounds.
notes: 2nd Street is now Maple Street; the grid north of it (3rd to 5th Streets and the extensions of A to E Streets) does not appear in the modern street data and was probably never built.
Placed from three junctions on 2nd Street (A, B and C Streets) as a helmert, which fixes scale and rotation but leaves the north-south position resting on the parcel centreline.

East Bound Brook and Beechwood Heights (Middlesex); 100 ft. Three parts: 1 grid north of 2nd Street (helmert on 2nd Street), 2 Harris, Fisher and Union Avenues (two points), 3 Main Street between D and E Streets (one detected, one hand-picked). All low confidence.

sheet-19-2.description: The lower left and middle of sheet 19, below the heavy dividing line, shows the part of the Borough of Middlesex between East Bound Brook and Dunellen, at 100 ft to an inch, with north towards the top. Harris Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right, marked as the road to Dunellen. At the left Union Avenue meets it from the south-west at the junction with Shepherd Avenue and Grant Avenue, and Fisher Avenue joins it from the north near the middle. North of Harris Avenue are a few scattered frame dwellings and sheds, a coop and an auto repair shop along the road, and the strip of a block marked 196. South of Harris Avenue are the Beechwood Heights Nurseries of Thos. Young, Jr., where long glass houses on concrete foundations stand in two groups with a shipping house, a coal house, a hose reel and store sheds, and a few outbuildings along the edge. The nursery is protected by a night watchman, with steam heat and electric light, and its hydrants are fed by 6 inch pipes. The sheet is marked No Exposure along the left edge. The detached block of Main Street at the lower right is a separate part.
notes: Placed from two junctions, Harris Avenue with Union, Grant and Shepherd Avenues and Harris Avenue with Fisher Avenue (a two-point helmert, low confidence).
Dunellen appears only in the label Road to Dunnellen, which is the spelling printed on the sheet.

East Bound Brook and Beechwood Heights (Middlesex); 100 ft. Three parts: 1 grid north of 2nd Street (helmert on 2nd Street), 2 Harris, Fisher and Union Avenues (two points), 3 Main Street between D and E Streets (one detected, one hand-picked). All low confidence.

sheet-19-3.description: A detached block at the lower right of sheet 19, enclosed by heavy lines, shows Main Street in East Bound Brook, Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, at 100 ft to an inch, with north towards the top. D Street runs north and south at the left edge and E Street at about three hundred feet to the right, where it ends at Main Street. The block bounded by D Street, E Street and Main Street is marked 13 and is empty, with a north arrow. East of E Street stand the Ulmer and Wagner Awning Factory, a one storey brick building with pilasters, and a building of the Pierce Estates marked 18, rented to state and federal agricultural departments. South of Main Street the Public Service Corporation sub-station, a concrete floor and fireproof building with steel girders, stands on the large block marked 464. The edges of the part are marked No Exposure, since the neighbouring ground is on other sheets. A 6 inch water pipe runs along the north side of Main Street.
notes: Main is now Walnut Street in the modern street data.
The junction of D Street and Main Street was detected; the junction with E Street was hand picked because E Street ends at Main Street and only one of its arms is drawn.
The block is a detached piece of the area shown on sheets 17 and 18; it is placed from two junctions 330 ft apart (helmert, low confidence).

East Bound Brook and Beechwood Heights (Middlesex); 100 ft. Three parts: 1 grid north of 2nd Street (helmert on 2nd Street), 2 Harris, Fisher and Union Avenues (two points), 3 Main Street between D and E Streets (one detected, one hand-picked). All low confidence.

sheet-20-1.description: Sheet 20 shows Beechwood Heights in the Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, at 100 ft to an inch, with north towards the upper left. Shepherd Avenue runs along the top, crossed by Beechwood Avenue at the left, Hazelwood Avenue and Norwood Avenue, and by Emerson Avenue at the right edge; sheet 21 continues to the right. Grant Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, meeting Elmwood Avenue and, further south, Union Avenue; Sherman Avenue curves from Hazelwood Avenue towards Elmwood Avenue. The blocks are laid out as long narrow lots, with detached frame dwellings and outbuildings spread thinly along the streets, many lots vacant and numbered along the avenues. Ambrose Brook runs along the lower edge below the Union Avenue bridge. Water pipes of 6 inch bore follow most streets, with fire hydrants marked DH. Heavy lines cut off the lower right corner of the sheet, where the Elizabeth Town Water Co. pumping station and a separate block of Union Avenue and Prospect Place are drawn as separate parts. The sheet is marked Beechwood Heights, entire sheet.
notes: Sherman Avenue is now Dorn Avenue in the modern street data; Norwood Avenue may be today's Nutwood Avenue.
Grant Avenue and the junctions on it were left out as control because they sit 4 to 8 m off their drawn positions.
Placed from five junctions on Shepherd, Hazelwood, Beechwood and Dorn Avenues; the fit is weaker towards the south.

Beechwood Heights (Middlesex); 100 ft. Part 1 main (Grant and Union Avenues left out as displaced; Sherman = Dorn Avenue); part 2 detached block (Union, Beechwood, Prospect Place), anchored; part 3 (triangle between the heavy lines: pumping station, Green Brook, steel bridge) not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: triangle between the heavy lines: pumping station, Green Brook, steel bridge (no street junction; needs hand-picked or parcel-corner control (step 6b)).

sheet-20-2.description: A detached block at the lower right of sheet 20, bounded by heavy lines on its north and west sides, shows Union Avenue, Beechwood Avenue and Prospect Place in Beechwood Heights, Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, at 100 ft to an inch, with north towards the upper left. Union Avenue runs from the upper right towards the lower left, and meets Beechwood Avenue, a short street running north to the heavy line, and Prospect Place, a long street running south between rows of narrow numbered lots. The lots along Prospect Place are built up with frame dwellings, outbuildings and small stores, numbered between 1 and 50 along the avenue, and a small building marked Beechwood Heights Fire Co. No. 1 stands at the top right beside lots numbered 602 to 614. A 36 inch water main runs along Union Avenue and 6 inch pipes follow Prospect Place. The lower right edge is marked No Exposure. The part has its own north arrow near the top right and is placed on the sheet away from the ground to which it belongs.
notes: Anchored on the single junction of Union Avenue, Beechwood Avenue and Prospect Place, with scale and rotation taken from part 1 of the sheet (low confidence).
The block between the heavy lines below it, with the Elizabeth Town Water Co. pumping station, Green Brook, Ambrose Brook and the steel bridge, has no street junction and was not placed.

Beechwood Heights (Middlesex); 100 ft. Part 1 main (Grant and Union Avenues left out as displaced; Sherman = Dorn Avenue); part 2 detached block (Union, Beechwood, Prospect Place), anchored; part 3 (triangle between the heavy lines: pumping station, Green Brook, steel bridge) not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: triangle between the heavy lines: pumping station, Green Brook, steel bridge (no street junction; needs hand-picked or parcel-corner control (step 6b)).

sheet-21.description: An outlying, thinly built sheet in the Beechwood Heights section of the Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. A heavy line runs down the sheet from top to bottom, bending once near the middle. West of it a long road lettered Union Av. runs from the junction of Green Brook Road, Bound Brook Road and a lane at the upper left down to the bottom of the sheet, crossed by Lawrence and by the unopened Valentine and Vail; long narrow lots run off it towards the left edge. East of the heavy line a second Union Av. runs the height of the sheet with Stout Av., Giles, Leonard, Howard and Lawrence leaving it to the east, Fisher Av. at the top right and Emerson Av. and Shepherd Av. near the bottom, where Grant Av. and Union Av. meet at the lower right. Several of these streets are marked not opened or not improved. The sheet is dominated by greenhouse florists: E. R. Finck and William Finck on the west side and Henry Schnitzspahn Jr. in the centre, each with long ranges of greenhouses and boiler houses. Other buildings are scattered dwellings, poultry houses, a milk bottling shed and a filling station on Bound Brook Road. The Watchung School, a brick building with steam heat, stands at Lawrence and Fisher Av. at the top right, and the Harris Lane Union Sunday School near Shepherd Av. at the bottom. The sheet is marked Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, entire sheet.
notes: Leonard is today's Cook Avenue and the Lawrence at the top right (meeting Fisher Avenue) is today's Lorraine Avenue (order and spacing along Union Avenue match OpenStreetMap).

The west half of the sheet (the western Union Av., Green Brook Road and Bound Brook Road junction, Lawrence, Valentine and Vail west of the heavy line) has no junction that survives in OpenStreetMap; the area is now a post-war subdivision (Dorn Avenue, Douglass Lane, Shearn Drive). Placement there rests on control in the east half only.
Watchung School at Lawrence (Lorraine Avenue) and Fisher Avenue; florists E. R. Finck, William Finck and Henry Schnitzspahn Jr.

Beechwood Heights, Borough of Middlesex; 100 ft; turned (north upper left). One part: the heavy line down the sheet is not a part divider. Leonard = Cook Avenue, Lawrence (top right) = Lorraine Avenue. West half (old Union Av, Green Brook Rd / Bound Brook Rd junction) has no surviving junction; placed from the east half (Union Avenue, Fisher, Emerson hand-picked).

sheet-22-1.description: The main part of sheet 22 covers the village of Lincoln in the Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, at 100 ft to an inch, with north towards the upper right. It takes in the blocks between Smalley Av. at the top and Lincoln Blvd. at the bottom, crossed by Drake Av. and Voorhees Av., and runs from Sherman Av. and the end of Harris Av. on the left past Mountain Av. in the middle to Sheridan Av. at the right edge. The blocks are laid out in regular narrow lots, mostly with small frame dwellings and outbuildings; many lots are still empty. On the Mountain Av. side are the fire department's Lincoln Hose Co. No. 1 and a white wash laundry. South of Lincoln Blvd., between the boulevard and the Central Railroad of New Jersey along the bottom of this part, lie a pole storage yard, the Carpenter and McKay lumber yard, a passenger station, the Chas. Ahr Co. cutlery factory, the Whitite Steel and Steel Castings Co. foundry, a ruined building with no roof and a cement block factory near the right edge. A curved siding runs from the main line into the lumber yard. The inset of Harris Av. and Smalley Av. occupies the upper left corner and is a separate part. The sheet is marked Lincoln, Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, entire sheet, and its edges refer to sheet 23 at the left.
notes: Sherman Avenue is today's Madison Avenue; Smalley Avenue is today's Pershing Avenue (West Pershing Avenue west of Mountain Avenue).
The sheet is drawn about 6 percent larger than its 100 ft scale (fitted 4.2 px/ft against about 4.0 for the atlas).
Chas. Ahr Co. cutlery factory; Whitite Steel and Steel Castings Co.; Carpenter and McKay lumber yard; Lincoln Hose Co. No. 1.

Lincoln, Borough of Middlesex; 100 ft; north upper right. Three parts: 1 main upper strip (Smalley to Lincoln Blvd, Sherman to Sheridan), 2 inset top left (Harris Av and Smalley Av, two churches), 3 lower strip below the heavy line (Voorhees and Lincoln Blvd east of Sheridan). Sherman = Madison Avenue, Smalley = Pershing / West Pershing Avenue, Grant = East Street, Lincoln Av = South Lincoln Avenue. Drawn about 6 percent large.

sheet-22-2.description: A small inset in the upper left corner of sheet 22, boxed off by heavy lines, drawn at the same 100 ft scale and nearly the same orientation as the main part. It shows the crossing of Harris Av., running diagonally across the inset, and Smalley Av., which leaves it towards the right, at the western edge of Lincoln in the Borough of Middlesex. Water pipes of 6 and 36 inches are drawn along Harris Av. Two churches are the reason for the inset: the Middlesex Union Chapel north of Smalley Av., a small frame building with furnace heat and electric light, and the Blessed Virgin Mary Roman Catholic Church south of Harris Av., a frame church with steam heat. A few dwellings, an office and an automobile shed stand on the remaining lots, and the inset carries its own north arrow. Its edges are marked no exposure on all sides, and block numbers 367, 377 and 426 are printed in it. The inset is placed from the one junction it shares with the modern street network, Harris Avenue and West Pershing Avenue, with the scale of the main part of the sheet.
notes: Smalley Avenue is today's West Pershing Avenue.
Placed from one junction (Harris Avenue / West Pershing Avenue) with the scale of part 1 and the rotation of the drawn streets; low confidence.
Middlesex Union Chapel; Blessed Virgin Mary R.C. Church.

Lincoln, Borough of Middlesex; 100 ft; north upper right. Three parts: 1 main upper strip (Smalley to Lincoln Blvd, Sherman to Sheridan), 2 inset top left (Harris Av and Smalley Av, two churches), 3 lower strip below the heavy line (Voorhees and Lincoln Blvd east of Sheridan). Sherman = Madison Avenue, Smalley = Pershing / West Pershing Avenue, Grant = East Street, Lincoln Av = South Lincoln Avenue. Drawn about 6 percent large.

sheet-22-3.description: The lower strip of sheet 22, below a heavy line, continues Lincoln in the Borough of Middlesex eastwards beyond Sheridan Av. at 100 ft to an inch, with north towards the upper right. It covers two rows of blocks along Voorhees Av. and Lincoln Blvd., from Sheridan Av. at the left edge past Grant Av., marked not opened, to the diagonal Lincoln Av. and on to the right edge. The upper row, north of Voorhees Av., and the row between Voorhees Av. and Lincoln Blvd. hold narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings, many still vacant. South of Lincoln Blvd., along the Central Railroad of New Jersey and the Philadelphia and Reading Railway at the bottom of the sheet, is a row of chemical and paint works: the Middlesex Aniline Co. chemical factory, where admittance was refused inside the buildings, vacant factory buildings formerly of the Globe Metal Polish Co., and the C. A. Leitch Mfg. Co., makers of paints, varnishes and floorings, with mixing, can storage and shipping buildings. Sidings leave the main line for these works. A scale bar is printed at the bottom left.
notes: Grant Avenue is today's East Street; Lincoln Avenue is today's South Lincoln Avenue.
Middlesex Aniline Co. chemical factory; C. A. Leitch Mfg. Co. paint and varnish works; Globe Metal Polish Co. (vacant).

Lincoln, Borough of Middlesex; 100 ft; north upper right. Three parts: 1 main upper strip (Smalley to Lincoln Blvd, Sherman to Sheridan), 2 inset top left (Harris Av and Smalley Av, two churches), 3 lower strip below the heavy line (Voorhees and Lincoln Blvd east of Sheridan). Sherman = Madison Avenue, Smalley = Pershing / West Pershing Avenue, Grant = East Street, Lincoln Av = South Lincoln Avenue. Drawn about 6 percent large.

sheet-23-1.description: The main part of sheet 23 covers the south-western end of Lincoln in the Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, at 100 ft to an inch, turned on the page so that north points to the upper left and Lincoln Blvd. runs up the sheet. On the left are two blocks between Voorhees Av. and Lincoln Blvd., divided by Sherman Av. and McKinley Av., with a few frame dwellings. East of Lincoln Blvd. a strip of works lines the boulevard: the Bound Brook Oil-less Bearing Co. with its foundry, machine shop, pattern storage and the Nigrum building, a lumber storage, and the long concrete buildings of the American Cement Tile Mfg. Co. Beyond them the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey and the parallel lines lettered P.R.R. and L.V.R.R. run the height of the sheet. East of the tracks lies the Snyder Engineering Co. storage yard, occupied by various contractors, with narrow gauge switch tracks, scattered storage sheds and T. P. Carlson's metal tank works, and at the top, along Mountain Av., the American Asphalt Paint Co. factory. Heavy lines on the right cut off three boxed areas drawn elsewhere: Lincoln Blvd. at Cedar Av. at the top right, a vacant former chemical plant and the Commercial Acetylene Supply Co. works; they are separate parts.
notes: Sherman Avenue is today's Madison Avenue.
Placed from four junctions at the corners of the two blocks west of Lincoln Boulevard; the railroad yards and the east half have no control of their own.
Bound Brook Oil-less Bearing Co.; American Cement Tile Mfg. Co.; Snyder Engineering Co. storage yard; American Asphalt Paint Co.

Lincoln, Borough of Middlesex; 100 ft; turned (north upper left). Four parts: 1 main (Voorhees Av and Lincoln Blvd, rail yards to Mountain Av), 2 top right box (Lincoln Blvd at Cedar Av), 3 middle right box (vacant former chemical plant, Private Rd, L.V.R.R.), 4 bottom right box (Commercial Acetylene Supply Co., L.V.R.R.). Parts 3 and 4 have no street and could not be located.

sheet-23-2.description: A boxed part in the upper right corner of sheet 23, at 100 ft to an inch and with the same orientation as the main part (north to the upper left). It continues Lincoln Blvd. south-west beyond the bottom of the main part, to its crossing with Cedar Av., which runs diagonally across the box and over the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, the line lettered P.R.R. and the Lehigh Valley Railroad at the right. Cedar Av. meets the boulevard with a small triangular island on its south side. The only works is the Dwight P. Robinson and Co. contractors storage yard between Lincoln Blvd. and the railroad, with a long storage shed, a shop, an office and machine shop and a few small sheds; a single dwelling stands in the lower left. The box is lettered Lincoln, Borough of Middlesex, Middlesex County, entire sheet, and the sheet's title cartouche sits in its upper right corner.

Dwight P. Robinson and Co. contractors storage.

Parts 3 and 4 have no street and could not be located.
